messages:
maya_cs: Quick week0 care-check for BlueHarbor private/VPC deploy. Two potential blockers: KMS key approval still pending (ticket SEC-4892) and outbound egress rule to partner CIDR not opened. Also customer says audit log samples not showing in their SIEM. Any updates?

aditya_se: Reached out to security. They want the key policy to include explicit usage restrictions (no decrypt for user-facing keys). Posted a draft in Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/cs/pages/BlueHarbor+KMS+Policy

linus_infra: I can open the egress once we have justification. @maya_cs please paste exact CIDR + ports. I have the firewall console ready.

maya_cs: CIDR 52.23.12.0/24 port 443 for partner API, and also 10.0.4.0/24 to allow their telemetry collector. Customer also asked for our KMS rotation schedule: rotation every 90 days, currently manual rotate disabled per customer request, retention 365d. I'll attach the schedule in the ticket.

sarah_cust: Customer confirmed manual rotation is ok. They want audit logs forwarded to Splunk at splunk.blueharbor.net:8088. They said initial samples from earlier this morning are missing. Raising as potential renewal signal: finance flagged onboarding pace — if unresolved >30 days mark as at-risk.

ollie_support: For audit-forwarding, check the forwarder config. Common issues: no forwarder service enabled or token misconfig. From infra, quick smoke command to validate connectivity:

```
curl -v -X POST https://splunk.blueharbor.net:8088/services/collector/event -H 'Authorization: Splunk <token>' -d '{"event":"test"}'
```

Also verify VPC Flow Logs are delivering to the customer's S3 prefix and that lifecycle policy isn't archiving immediately.

opsbot: Deploy bot: priv-deploy/blueharbor v1.0.3 smoke tests started at 1765554350. status: partial-success. failed-tests: audit-forwarding

linus_infra: Pushed firewall rule id fw-7a9 for 52.23.12.0/24:443 and 10.0.4.0/24:443. Changes should be live in ~5m. @maya_cs ask customer to retry splunk curl after 5m.

maya_cs: Pinging BlueHarbor now. One more question from them: they need an IAM role for cross-account read for logs ingestion. Do we create role in their account or provide role in ours?

aditya_se: Best practice is role in their account with trust to redwood-infra role. I'll prepare a CFN snippet for IAM role 'redwood-priv-BlueHarbor-Logs' with a ReadS3Logs policy and cross-account trust. Will post by EOD. Sample trust snippet I'll include:

```
Type: AWS::IAM::Role
Properties:
  RoleName: redwood-priv-BlueHarbor-Logs
  AssumeRolePolicyDocument: ... (Trust redwood-deploy-account)
  Policies: - PolicyName: ReadS3Logs
    PolicyDocument: ...
```

sarah_cust: Noting renewal risk: customer called out timeline concerns. If KMS approval + logs not resolved within 72h, escalate to AM/Finance for renewal outreach. Adding to renewal tracker.

maya_cs: Action items summary: @aditya_se prepare CFN for IAM by EOD; @linus_infra confirm egress live in 10m; @maya_cs to push KMS policy draft to security and cc @sarah_cust; @ollie_support to rerun audit-forwarding smoke after firewall change and post results. I'll follow up tomorrow AM. :thumbsup:

ollie_support: Copy, will rerun smoke and attach logs (grep and archive). last smoke run id smoke-1765554380, logs will be uploaded to ticket SEC-4892.

opsbot: Reminder: next check-in scheduled 1765630000 (week1). Reaction :calendar:
